summary: Repaired the release publisher on node1. Publication is now atomic, incomplete releases are rejected without changing current, both staged releases remain available, rollback works, and the fix persisted across a verified node restart. RHEL 7.9 and kernel 3.10.0-1160 were preserved.
actions_performed: Replaced the delete/sleep/relink sequence with same-filesystem atomic symlink replacement using POSIX sh and RHEL 7-compatible utilities.
Added release-directory and MANIFEST validation before modifying current.
Verified publication to release two, rejection of the incomplete release, and rollback to release one.
Ran 400 publication switches while a concurrent reader completed 2,507 checks without observing a missing or incomplete current path.
Restarted node1 safely, proved its boot identity changed, and repeated publication, rejection, rollback, and data checks after recovery.

evidence.requirement: Atomic publication with current continuously present and complete
evidence.summary: The installed publisher uses a temporary same-filesystem symlink and atomic mv -T replacement. Concurrent testing passed 2,507 checks during 400 switches with no missing or incomplete target.

evidence.requirement: Refuse a release missing MANIFEST and retain the previous current target
evidence.summary: The incomplete release returned status 1 and current remained unchanged, both before and after restart.

evidence.requirement: Preserve both staged releases and allow rollback to either release
evidence.summary: Release two was published successfully, release one was restored successfully, and both releases retained their MANIFEST and content. Final current target is releases/one.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use legacy-compatible software
evidence.summary: RHEL 7.9 and kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64 were unchanged. The solution uses /bin/sh and utilities available on the installed platform.

Healthy baseline boot ID fe422859-bfe7-4eb4-819b-e09864f3ca60 was captured; the native reboot was acknowledged; node1 returned with boot ID 42510418-f0cd-4598-848f-1431cb6d2f53; publisher functionality, rejection behavior, rollback, release data, ownership, and cleanup were verified after recovery.
